events.title: BlackRock Advisors settles SEC conflict-disclosure action
events.summary: The adviser accepted a $12 million penalty and compliance review over undisclosed portfolio-manager conflicts.
events.limitations: Settled administrative findings; neither admission nor criminal conviction.

events.title: BlackRock settles whistleblower-award waiver action
events.summary: SEC ordered a $340,000 penalty over separation agreements waiving whistleblower awards.
events.limitations: No identified instance of a prevented SEC communication or enforcement of the clause.

events.title: BlackRock Advisors settles fund-disclosure case
events.summary: SEC imposed a $2.5 million penalty for inaccurate Aviron investment descriptions and interest-rate reporting.
events.limitations: The adviser corrected disclosures in 2019; no admission or denial.

events.title: NVIDIA settles SEC cryptomining-disclosure action
events.summary: NVIDIA accepted a $5.5 million penalty concerning two fiscal-2018 quarterly reports.
events.limitations: Concerns securities disclosure, not AI model safety.

events.title: FTC files Ring privacy and security allegations
events.summary: FTC alleged excessive internal video access, algorithm training without consent and inadequate account security.
events.limitations: Complaint allegations resolved by consent order, not tried findings.

events.title: Court enters Ring privacy consent order
events.summary: The order requires $5.8 million, security safeguards and deletion of defined recordings and derived work products.
events.limitations: Specific deletion categories and exceptions are defined in the order.

events.title: Alexa privacy settlement announced
events.summary: DOJ and FTC alleged excessive retention and ineffective deletion of children’s voice and other user data.
events.limitations: Use of retained data in algorithm improvement was an agency allegation.

events.title: Court enters Alexa privacy consent order
events.summary: FTC’s docket records entry of the settlement governing deletion, data uses and a $25 million penalty.

events.title: Facebook agrees to $5 billion privacy settlement
events.summary: The agreement resolved FTC allegations that Facebook violated its 2012 privacy order.
events.limitations: Cambridge Analytica enforcement was related but separate.

events.title: FTC finalizes Facebook privacy-order modification
events.summary: FTC approved the revised administrative privacy order incorporating the 2019 settlement.
events.limitations: Later proposed modifications are separate proceedings.

events.title: Microsoft announces Xbox privacy settlement
events.summary: The $20 million agreement addressed FTC allegations about children’s account data, consent and retention.
events.limitations: FTC’s 2024 update confirms court entry and payment; this date is the announcement.

events.title: Court finds Google unlawfully maintained search monopolies
events.summary: The court found Sherman Act liability in general search services and general search text advertising.
events.limitations: Civil trial finding; subsequent appeals are included below.

events.title: Google search remedies enter final district-court judgment
events.summary: The judgment imposes distribution restrictions, qualified data access and syndication duties.
events.limitations: Final district-court judgment does not mean appeals are exhausted.

events.title: Court denies Google’s partial stay request without prejudice
events.summary: The court declined to pause data-sharing and syndication provisions at that stage, permitting a renewed request after advance notice.
events.limitations: A stay ruling is not an appellate decision on liability.

events.title: United States files Google search cross-appeal brief
events.summary: The government filed a response and opening cross-appeal brief in D.C. Circuit cases 26-5023, 26-5047 and 26-5049.
events.limitations: Party arguments are not appellate findings.

events.title: Amazon Prime settlement enters court order
events.summary: Amazon’s consent settlement provides a $1 billion penalty, $1.5 billion redress fund and enrollment/cancellation changes.
events.limitations: Neither admission nor denial; separate from Amazon’s antitrust case.

events.title: Amazon Prime refund procedure is revised
events.summary: The revised order expands automatic payments and conditionally permits supplemental distributions capped at $200 total per eligible consumer.
events.limitations: The cap is not a guarantee that every consumer receives $200; conditions and phases apply.

events.title: Palantir hiring-discrimination settlement announced
events.summary: DOL announced a consent decree providing $1,659,434 in relief and eight job offers.
events.limitations: Palantir denied the allegations; this was a settlement, not a contested merits judgment.

relationships.label: Settled conflict-disclosure findings
relationships.context: SEC imposed a $12 million penalty and compliance relief on the adviser.
relationships.limitations: Settled administrative findings; BlackRock Advisors neither admitted nor denied them.

relationships.label: Settled whistleblower-rule findings
relationships.context: BlackRock, Inc. settled the SEC award-waiver action for $340,000.
relationships.limitations: No admission or denial; SEC found no instance of prevented communication or clause enforcement.

relationships.label: Settled inaccurate fund-disclosure findings
relationships.context: SEC imposed a $2.5 million penalty for fund-disclosure inaccuracies.
relationships.limitations: BlackRock Advisors neither admitted nor denied findings; disclosures were corrected in 2019.

relationships.label: Settled securities-disclosure findings
relationships.context: SEC order concerns two fiscal-2018 quarterly reports and imposed $5.5 million.
relationships.limitations: NVIDIA neither admitted nor denied findings. This is not an AI-safety or criminal judgment.

relationships.label: Privacy and security consent settlement
relationships.context: Entered order imposes privacy/security duties and a $5.8 million judgment.
relationships.limitations: Ring neither admitted nor denied allegations; underlying conduct was not tried.

relationships.label: Acquired Ring
relationships.context: FTC identifies Amazon’s February 2018 acquisition of Ring as background.
relationships.limitations: Corporate ownership alone does not establish responsibility for each alleged practice.

relationships.label: Alexa privacy consent settlement
relationships.context: DOJ pursued the FTC’s Alexa privacy allegations; the court entered the consent order in July 2023.
relationships.limitations: Amazon denied violations; this service-specific settlement does not adjudicate unrelated AWS practices.

relationships.label: Privacy consent settlement
relationships.context: Facebook accepted a $5 billion privacy settlement concerning its 2012 FTC order.
relationships.limitations: Neither admission nor denial. Cambridge Analytica proceedings and later Meta disputes are separate.

relationships.label: Xbox children’s privacy settlement
relationships.context: Xbox children’s-data settlement; the FTC later confirmed entry and payment of $20 million.
relationships.limitations: No-admission stipulation; Microsoft said a retention glitch was corrected. No finding about unrelated products.

relationships.label: Civil monopolization finding
relationships.context: Trial finding concerns general search services and general search text advertising.
relationships.limitations: Google disputes liability; 2026 appeal and cross-appeals are documented. No appellate disposition verified here.

relationships.label: Prime enrollment and cancellation settlement
relationships.context: Entered Prime consent order provides a civil penalty, consumer redress and interface changes.
relationships.limitations: Defendants neither admitted nor denied allegations; separate Amazon antitrust litigation is outside this record.

relationships.label: Hiring-discrimination consent decree
relationships.context: OFCCP consent decree concerns three engineering job categories and provides monetary relief and job offers.
relationships.limitations: Palantir denied discrimination and disputed the statistical analysis; no contested merits judgment.

cases.title: BlackRock Advisors: undisclosed outside-business conflict
cases.summary: SEC settlement concerning a portfolio manager’s outside energy business.
cases.findings: SEC found undisclosed conflicts and deficient controls involving the manager’s Rice Energy interest and a fund investment.
cases.response: The adviser neither admitted nor denied the findings.
cases.outcome: $12 million penalty, censure, cease-and-desist relief and independent compliance review.
cases.limitations: The respondent was BlackRock Advisors, LLC. The order does not establish criminal guilt or misconduct by unrelated group companies.

cases.title: BlackRock: separation agreements and whistleblower incentives
cases.summary: SEC action over award-waiver language used from 2011 to 2016.
cases.findings: SEC found that award waivers undermined incentives for reporting potential securities violations.
cases.response: BlackRock neither admitted nor denied findings; it had revised the agreement before SEC staff contacted it.
cases.outcome: $340,000 civil penalty and remedial measures, including annual training.
cases.limitations: SEC identified no instance in which the clause stopped a communication or BlackRock enforced it. No criminal finding.

cases.title: BlackRock Advisors: Aviron investment disclosures
cases.summary: SEC order addresses publicly filed fund reports from 2015–2019.
cases.findings: SEC found that reports misclassified film-finance business Aviron and overstated its interest rate.
cases.response: BlackRock neither admitted nor denied findings. It identified and corrected the inaccuracies in 2019.
cases.outcome: $2.5 million penalty, censure and cease-and-desist order.
cases.limitations: This disclosure action is distinct from the separate case against Aviron’s founder. It does not attribute his misconduct to the adviser.

cases.title: NVIDIA: cryptomining’s effect on gaming revenue
cases.summary: SEC found omissions about a material driver of GPU revenue growth.
cases.findings: The order found inadequate disclosure and controls concerning cryptomining demand in two fiscal-2018 quarters.
cases.response: NVIDIA consented without admitting or denying the findings.
cases.outcome: $5.5 million civil penalty and cease-and-desist order.
cases.limitations: The cited Securities Act provisions can rest on negligence; this is not a criminal conviction or resolution of separate investor litigation.

cases.title: Ring: private videos, algorithm training and account security
cases.summary: Court-approved settlement of FTC privacy and security allegations.
cases.findings: FTC alleged unauthorized video access and training uses, alongside security failures; these allegations were resolved without trial.
cases.response: Ring neither admitted nor denied the allegations and waived appeal of the consent order.
cases.outcome: $5.8 million judgment; privacy/security program and deletion of defined pre-March-2018 recordings and affected models or algorithms.
cases.limitations: The decree establishes obligations, not criminal guilt. It does not implicate every employee or all later Ring products.

cases.title: Amazon Alexa: children’s recordings and deletion requests
cases.summary: Entered settlement addressing retention and deletion of Alexa data.
cases.statusDetail: Court entry verified in FTC docket, July 19, 2023.
cases.findings: The complaint alleged COPPA and deception violations, including retention after deletion requests and use to improve algorithms.
cases.response: Amazon denied violating the law and described parental controls and planned deletion changes.
cases.outcome: $25 million penalty, deletion requirements, a ban on using information covered by deletion requests to develop or improve data products, and privacy-program obligations.
cases.limitations: Settlement of disputed allegations, not a trial finding. The case does not adjudicate Amazon’s unrelated services.

cases.title: Facebook: privacy controls and the 2019 FTC settlement
cases.summary: $5 billion agreement addressing alleged violations of an earlier privacy order.
cases.statusDetail: Settlement announced in 2019; FTC order modification finalized April 28, 2020.
cases.findings: FTC alleged deceptive privacy settings, third-party app access and misrepresentations concerning facial recognition and advertising uses.
cases.response: Facebook neither admitted nor denied allegations; its statement acknowledged a breach of trust and promised stronger privacy controls.
cases.outcome: $5 billion civil penalty and strengthened privacy governance, independent oversight and certifications.
cases.limitations: Cambridge Analytica was separately prosecuted administratively. This case does not establish every Cambridge Analytica allegation or decide later Meta disputes.

cases.title: Microsoft Xbox: children’s account data
cases.summary: COPPA settlement covering notice, parental consent and retention.
cases.statusDetail: Announced June 2023; FTC’s 2024 update confirms an entered federal order and payment.
cases.findings: FTC alleged premature collection, incomplete notices and excessive retention of children’s personal data.
cases.response: No-admission terms appear in the stipulation. Microsoft said it fixed a retention glitch, deleted data and strengthened controls.
cases.outcome: $20 million penalty and changes to consent, deletion and disclosures to game publishers.
cases.limitations: Microsoft’s glitch explanation is its response, not the entirety of FTC’s allegations. No criminal finding or ruling on unrelated Microsoft products.

cases.title: Google: search-distribution monopolization
cases.summary: Civil trial findings followed by remedies and appellate proceedings.
cases.statusDetail: District-court liability and December 2025 judgment; 2026 appeal and cross-appeals documented. No appellate disposition verified here.
cases.findings: The court found unlawful monopoly maintenance in general search services and general search text advertising.
cases.response: Google disputes the decision, emphasizing product quality, user choice and competition, and appealed in January 2026.
cases.outcome: Distribution restrictions and data-sharing/syndication remedies; May 2026 partial-stay request denied without prejudice.
cases.limitations: Do not call this an unappealable final outcome. The government’s July 2026 brief is advocacy. The separate ad-tech case is outside this record.

cases.title: Amazon Prime: enrollment and cancellation
cases.summary: Consent settlement over allegedly deceptive subscription flows.
cases.statusDetail: Entered September 2025 order; redress procedure revised September 2026.
cases.findings: FTC alleged enrollment without informed consent and deliberately difficult cancellation processes.
cases.response: The order states defendants neither admit nor deny the complaint allegations.
cases.outcome: $1 billion civil penalty, $1.5 billion consumer-redress fund and interface changes; later order expands automatic refunds.
cases.limitations: Consumer eligibility and supplemental payments are conditional. This settlement does not decide the separate Amazon antitrust action or imply all subscriptions were unauthorized.

cases.title: Palantir: engineering-applicant hiring practices
cases.summary: Consent decree resolving OFCCP’s historical hiring-discrimination allegations.
cases.statusDetail: DOL announced the consent decree April 25, 2017.
cases.findings: OFCCP alleged race-based adverse impact against Asian applicants for three engineering job categories at Palo Alto.
cases.response: Palantir denied the allegations and offered alternative statistical analyses disputing adverse impact.
cases.outcome: $1,659,434 in back wages and other relief, including stock-option value, plus eight offers of employment.
cases.limitations: Resolved by consent, not a litigated discrimination finding. Historical executive-order duties must not be presented as a statement of current policy.

coverage.title: Corporate cases: documented actions and contested claims
coverage.scope: Eleven selected SEC, FTC, DOJ, court and DOL matters involving finance, technology, privacy and employment. Case dates identify specific actions. Company responses and later developments are recorded separately.
limits: This selection is not a comprehensive corporate misconduct database. Absence does not establish a clean record.
Regulatory findings, allegations, consent settlements and trial findings have different meanings. A documented settlement does not make every complaint allegation a proved fact.
No liability is inferred from attendance, investments, employment, corporate-group membership or other relationships.
BlackRock Advisors and BlackRock, Inc. are distinct respondents. Amazon’s existing atlas entity combines the parent and AWS; case roles specify services and defendants.
Google’s judgment is under documented appellate challenge; this edition verifies filings rather than asserting an exhausted appellate outcome.
Cases on AI suppliers can concern securities or employment rather than AI itself. Alexa and Ring have specific algorithm/data-use allegations.
Primary DOL decree indexed text was available, but direct PDF retrieval returned 403; the limitation is recorded in the source entry.
No private complainant identities, contact details, raw customer data or personal victim records are reproduced.
